speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the location and nature of your headache, and have you noticed any specific visual disturbances like blind spots or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any pain or tenderness when chewing or touching the scalp, and have you noticed any jaw claudication? I also need to check if you have any scalp sensitivity or shoulder pain.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: I strongly disagree with the previous assessment, as your presentation of headache and vision loss in a 69-year-old is classic for Giant Cell Arteritis, not Tuberculosis. Let me examine your temporal arteries for tenderness or thickening immediately. REQUEST TEST: ESR

speaker: Doctor
text: It is highly unusual for Giant Cell Arteritis to present with a normal ESR, so I must reconsider the differential diagnosis. Do you have any history of diabetes or hypertension, and have you noticed any swelling or pain in your jaw or temples?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal ESR and lack of classic GCA symptoms, I need to rule out intracranial pathology or vascular causes. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with contrast shows no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, mass lesion, or large vessel vasculitis. However, there are subtle signs of posterior circulation ischemia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience jaw pain when chewing or tenderness over your temples, and have you noticed any scalp sensitivity? I need to rule out Giant Cell Arteritis despite the normal ESR, as the posterior circulation findings are concerning. REQUEST TEST: Temporal Artery Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: With GCA effectively ruled out by the normal biopsy and ESR, the posterior circulation ischemia on MRI suggests a vascular etiology for your vision loss and headache. I need to evaluate the patency of your vertebral and basilar arteries to check for stenosis or occlusion. REQUEST TEST: MRA Head and Neck

speaker: Doctor
text: Since vascular and inflammatory causes have been ruled out, I suspect the vision loss and headache may be due to a primary ocular issue like increased intraocular pressure or a retinal condition. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive Ophthalmologic Exam with Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Visual Acuity: Right Eye 20/120, Left Eye 20/80. Fundoscopy: Findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of retinal hemorrhages confirm a vascular occlusion event rather than an inflammatory or mass lesion. Since we have ruled out Giant Cell Arteritis and large vessel stenosis, I suspect this is a branch retinal vein occlusion secondary to your underlying hypertension and hyperlipidemia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion
